topic: Mission 1 tuning: human says the first map is 'actually impossible' and must be super easy - choose the mechanism
context: HUMAN DIRECTIVE (verbatim): 'the first map should be super easy and it is actually impossible'; clarified 07:53 as: currently broken/unwinnable for the player -> fix it and make it super easy. This proposal decides HOW; that it must happen is fixed by the human.

CURRENT TUNING MACHINERY: difficulty tiers squire/knight/warlord (defs.py:438-451) scale enemy hp/dmg (world.py:170-174), AI income (ai.py:41), first wave (ai.py:35), wave size (ai.py:113), cap (ai.py:57,116,148); starting resources from difficulty (world.py:99-100). Default CLI difficulty is squire (app.py:1018). Two dead knobs exist that a campaign could own: generate_map(difficulty=...) is never read (mapgen.py:84) and the tier key 'speed' has no consumer anywhere.

EXISTING HARD-DIFFICULTY EVIDENCE (mimo's own balance runs, 3x, commit a7c3cc6 and design/notes): the Knight-tier hero dies inside wave 1 at 5:37-5:39. Fresh autoplay runs at all three tiers (headless, 1 run each) are being collected into .council/evidence/difficulty-map1.md before resolution - that file will state whether ANY tier is currently winnable by autoplay on the base map.

CONSTRAINTS: mission 1 must be 'impossible to lose' while still teaching build/gather/fight; skirmish must keep its three tiers (mimo owns balance); whatever mechanism wins should be data-driven so later campaign maps can ramp difficulty without new code.
reversibility: one commit; tuning lives in one data table (mission override / tier entry), revert restores today's behaviour

replies.evidence: .council/evidence/difficulty-map1.md — knight = no-win stalemate (DEFEAT 12:24 with Necropolis 5200/5200), warlord auto-loss 5:03, hero never revives (no Altar placed, world.py:1516-1522), squire 'win' is an AI threat early-return bug (ai.py:96-107 suppresses waves), and all runs used a QA-boosted start a real player does not get
replies.objection: map-1 easing must ALSO fix the two structural bugs or it stays fake-easy: (1) no Altar at start = hero permanently dead on first death, (2) ai.manage threat early-return makes waves binary (never if you attack, always if you turtle). Fixing those changes the intended difficulty gradient and is balance scope = mimo's call.

replies.evidence: human answered as mimo at 08:15: 'novice-tier' (rejecting deepseek's mission-override-easy). mimo's condition: fix the two structural bugs first (no-Altar hero revive; ai.py:96-107 threat early-return) or the ease is fake.
replies.objection: mission-override-easy creates a second parallel difficulty system: QA would have to test mission overrides x 3 tiers; the tested DIFFICULTY pipeline already exists (defs.py:438-451, consumers world.py:99/170, ai.py:35/41/113) and one more tier is data, not code.
replies.attribution: human speaking as mimo (mimo session absent; human chose 'You reply as mimo now' at 08:15)

debates.claim: against novice-tier: DIFFICULTY is drawn straight into the skirmish picker (ui.py:260 iterates DIFFICULTY.items()), so a 4th tier leaks into skirmish and rewrites the locked 3-tier design (DESIGN.md:87-88); and a global tier cannot make MISSION 1 'impossible to lose' — the campaign needs per-mission knobs anyway for maps 2..8+ (escalating boss/wave ramps), so one mechanism should serve both instead of two.
debates.evidence: ui.py:260-269; DESIGN.md:87-88; .council/evidence/survey-architecture.md (no per-map config plumbing exists)

debates.claim: against mission-override-easy: a second parallel difficulty system doubles the QA matrix (mission override x 3 tiers) in mimo's gate, while one extra DIFFICULTY entry is pure data wired through the already-tested consumers; and both of us agree the sequencing: fix the no-Altar revive (world.py:1516-1522) and the ai threat early-return (ai.py:96-107) BEFORE any tuning, or 'super easy' is an artifact of broken systems, not balance.
debates.evidence: human-as-mimo selections 08:15: 'novice-tier' + 'Fix bugs before tuning'; .council/evidence/difficulty-map1.md root causes 2 and 3
